summary: Final recommendations are now based on semantic review of the actual JD rather than mechanical score. Titles are treated only as hints: systems/inference/distributed work can rank highly without ML wording, while attractive titles are rejected when the detailed requirements conflict with May 2027 eligibility, experience level, work authorization, or the candidate's actual ownership. GitHub automation now produces a review queue and no longer overwrites this file.

changes_today.reason: Automated scoring is recall-only. It writes data/model_review_queue.json; Apply Now remains a separately reviewed artifact.
Despite the attractive graduate/ML title, the official JD requires a PhD. The BS/MS Graduate Quantitative Researcher is the eligible IMC track instead.
Excellent 2027 timing and systems/GPU content, but the official posting requires U.S.-person ITAR status.
Very strong GPU-cloud/Kubernetes fit, but the official JD explicitly says applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without visa sponsorship.
Near-perfect technical keyword match, but the official JD asks for 5+ years of industry experience, so it is not an appropriate new-grad recommendation.

recommendations.category: APPLY FIRST · CONFIRMED NEW GRAD · SYSTEMS
recommendations.location: San Francisco, CA (4 days/week in office)
recommendations.reason: The JD is unusually aligned even though the title is generic: Daft distributed query engine, GPU-cluster workloads, profiling/benchmarking, dataloading/storage/indexing, Python/Rust, and explicit preference for distributed systems / ML infrastructure / GPU-HPC backgrounds. This maps directly to the candidate's distributed-systems research, LLM inference work, profiling/performance analysis, Linux, and C++/Python strengths.
recommendations.new_grad: Explicit New Grad; candidates within about one year of graduating or recently graduated are welcomed.
recommendations.sponsorship: Not stated on the accessible official posting; no explicit sponsorship veto found.
recommendations.caveat: Compensation is below the highest-paying quant/large-tech options, but the technical match is substantially stronger than most generic SWE roles. Rust is helpful but not required because Python/C++/Go are also accepted.

recommendations.category: APPLY SOON · HIGH FIT · TIMING TO VERIFY
recommendations.reason: The actual JD is much more relevant than the generic title suggests: large-scale distributed systems, the full model-delivery pipeline from training through serving, online-model performance, and model-delivery optimization. It explicitly targets 0-2 years and values C++/Python/Go. This fits distributed training/inference, performance work, systems debugging, and software fundamentals well.
recommendations.new_grad: Early-career 0-2 years, but the posting does not state a May/August 2027 start window.
recommendations.sponsorship: The application asks candidates whether sponsorship is needed; the posting does not state an explicit no-sponsorship policy.
recommendations.caveat: Main uncertainty is start timing: it is an early-career opening rather than a labeled 2027 campus role. Do not represent availability earlier than the actual graduation date.

recommendations.reason: The JD directly names distributed infrastructure for multi-GPU LLM training, profiling and optimizing training/inference code, efficient LLM serving, CUDA, distributed-training frameworks, and vLLM. This is one of the cleanest matches for the candidate's inference, multi-GPU/distributed, performance, NCCL-adjacent and systems work.
recommendations.new_grad: Junior role; BS/MS accepted and internships, master's research, or substantial projects count as practical experience. Exact 2027 start timing is not stated.
recommendations.sponsorship: Not stated; no explicit no-sponsorship/citizenship restriction found on the official posting.
recommendations.caveat: The role also expects practical deep-learning competence. Lead with systems/inference work and describe model-framework ownership precisely rather than overstating PyTorch/model-training ownership.

recommendations.salary: Not reliably visible in the accessible posting
recommendations.reason: The JD accepts 1-3 years with internships counting and asks for GenAI/ML systems, Python/C++, an ML framework or vLLM/SGLang, inference-focused evaluations, and latency/throughput awareness. That is much closer to the candidate's actual inference/performance work than several generic new-grad software roles.
recommendations.new_grad: Early-career by requirements; internships count toward the stated 1-3 years. Exact 2027 graduation/start window is not stated.
recommendations.sponsorship: Not stated in the accessible posting.
recommendations.urgency: APPLY IF START DATE CAN MATCH
recommendations.caveat: Stretch because the role expects hands-on ML/inference experimentation, and start timing is not explicit. Emphasize vLLM/inference/performance work; do not claim ownership of model-training code that was done by collaborators.

recommendations.fit: High technical fit, more ambitious than a standard new-grad role
recommendations.reason: Unlike Sciforium's 5+ year distributed-training role, this JD does not state a years-of-experience minimum. It spans distributed pretraining, fault-tolerant training infrastructure, agent/eval environments, inference throughput/latency, serving pipelines, and GPU/runtime profiling. The candidate has credible overlap through distributed-system planning, LLM inference, performance analysis and agent/evaluation work.
recommendations.new_grad: MS/PhD required; no explicit years minimum, but it is not labeled new grad and exact 2027 start timing is not stated.
recommendations.sponsorship: Not stated on the accessible official posting.
recommendations.caveat: Do not pitch as a model-training specialist. The strongest story is systems/inference/evaluation; the role's pretraining and post-training tracks may expect deeper direct framework ownership than the candidate currently has.

recommendations.location: San Francisco or New York City (on-site)
recommendations.reason: The JD explicitly covers agentic LLM systems, retrieval pipelines, structured tool use, chained workflows, evaluation frameworks, failure modes, monitoring and observability. This is a direct match for the candidate's production AI-agent/tooling and evaluation work, even though it is less aligned with low-level distributed runtime research.
recommendations.new_grad: Explicit Early Career and accepts coursework/projects/internships; exact 2027 start date is not stated.
recommendations.sponsorship: Not stated; no explicit veto found on the official posting.
recommendations.caveat: This is product/agent engineering rather than core training/runtime. Five-day in-office requirement is material.

recommendations.fit: Strong quantitative alternative; less direct MLSys overlap
recommendations.reason: This is the correct IMC graduate research role for a BS/MS candidate. It values rigorous quantitative reasoning, programming and research/problem solving, which match the candidate's math/CS background and competitive-programming strength. It is not an ML-systems role, but compensation and exact 2027 timing make it worth keeping as a separate high-value track.
recommendations.new_grad: Exact eligibility: graduating September 2026-July 2027; February or August 2027 full-time start.
recommendations.sponsorship: The official application explicitly asks about current and future immigration sponsorship needs rather than stating a no-sponsorship veto.
recommendations.caveat: Do not confuse this with IMC Graduate Machine Learning Researcher, which requires a PhD. Interview preparation is substantially more probability/statistics/quant-focused than MLSys preparation.
recommendations.application_limit: IMC says one application per role per year and strongly encourages focusing on the role that best matches the candidate.
